import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Toronto spaces

A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.

It is conjectured that every T2, Toronto space is discrete.
W.R. Brian proved that this holds under GCH.

*References:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_space)
 - [The Toronto problem](https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf) by *W.R. Brian*
-/

namespace Toronto

open Cardinal

variable (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]

/-- A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.
-/
class TorontoSpace where
  toronto : ∀ ⦃Y : Set X⦄, #Y = #X → Y ≃ₜ X

/-- Every finite space is Toronto, since
the only subspace with same cardinality is the space itself.
-/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance Finite.torontoSpace [Finite X] : TorontoSpace X where
  toronto := by
    intro Y hY
    have eq : Y = Set.univ := by
      refine (Set.eq_univ_iff_ncard Y).mpr ?_
      have : Y.ncard = (#↑Y).toNat := by
        exact rfl
      rw [this, hY]
      exact rfl
    rw [eq]
    exact Homeomorph.Set.univ X

/-- Any T2, Toronto space is discrete. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem DiscreteTopology.of_t2_of_torontoSpace [T2Space X] [TorontoSpace X] :
    DiscreteTopology X := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add implication that this holds under the GCH

end Toronto

reformulations.difference: The class bundles a chosen homeomorphism for every full-cardinality subspace, rather than merely asserting existence. It includes the whole space, whereas Wikipedia's definition mentions proper subspaces.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved Nonempty (Toronto.TorontoSpace X) ↔ ∀ Y : Set X, Y ≠ Set.univ → #Y = #X → Nonempty (X ≃ₜ Y). In one direction, invert the bundled homeomorphisms. Conversely, use classical choice for proper subspaces and Homeomorph.Set.univ for the whole space. Brian's introduction itself includes all subspaces. The proof is in /workspace/review/proper-subspaces.lean and has no sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The theorem asserts discreteness for all cardinalities, without the uncountability restriction appearing in Wikipedia's counterexample formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite Hausdorff spaces are discrete. A countably infinite Hausdorff space has an infinite discrete subspace; that subspace has the same cardinality, so the Toronto property makes the whole space discrete. Consequently, universal discreteness is equivalent to nonexistence of an uncountable nondiscrete Hausdorff Toronto space. Both the countable case and this equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/countable-equivalence.lean without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf — W. R. Brian, The Toronto problem; especially the introduction, Proposition 2.6, and Corollary 6.2.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The finite instance is sorry-free, including empty and singleton cases; its use of ncard is protected by [Finite X], so the infinite-cardinality default does not affect it. Additional Lean tests constructed Toronto structures on arbitrary discrete spaces and showed that a two-point indiscrete space is Toronto but not discrete, while the usual real line is not Toronto. Brian distinguishes the original ℵ₁ problem from the general-cardinality question also discussed in his introduction; this file states the latter. Proposition 2.6 establishes only the GCH-conditional result, consistent with the unconditional theorem's research-open status. All scratch files compile successfully, and the reviewed file matches the committed version.
